title: Live imaging of the Drosophila ovarian germline stem cell niche
protocol: Collect and set up a cross of 20-30 virgin females and 5-10 males at 25°C in a vial with standard fly food.
Transfer flies to a new vial every 1-2 days until the day of dissection.
Ensure that the males kept with the females are wildtype if genetic perturbations could affect male reproduction.
Supplement the food with dry yeast, optionally, to boost reproduction.
Maintain flies for 3-5 days prior to dissection.
Dissect ovaries and mount them for observation.
Preheat 5 mL SIM, 1 mL fSIM, and 2 mL iSIM to 37°C.
Set up a 6-well plate with 3× wells containing 500 μL SIM for fly washes prior to dissection.
Prepare 2× wells on a glass dissection dish with 500 μL SIM for dissection.
Add one well with 200 μL fSIM.
Anesthetize the flies by pumping CO2 into the vial or incubating at 4°C for 5 minutes until they fall to the bottom of the vial.
Take 2–3 females carefully without getting them stuck in yeast paste.
Euthanize the flies by submerging them in 70% ethanol for 1 minute.
Wash the flies for 1 minute in each of the first three wells of SIM.
Transfer the flies to the fourth well of SIM and dissect the ovaries of all the flies.
Turn the female on her back.
Use forceps to pull at the ovipositor and remove the posterior of the abdomen.
If ovaries do not remain attached, lightly pinch the abdomen to dislodge them.
Transfer the ovaries to a final well of SIM for microdissection of individual ovarioles.
Use an eyelash tool to comb through the ovaries to break through the overlying muscle sheath.
Tease apart the individual ovarioles.
Sever the muscle sheath connected at the anterior tip of the terminal filament or most posterior egg chamber using an eyelash glued to a toothpick.
Remove as much muscle sheath as possible from the ovarioles.
Transfer 5–10 ovarioles in 10 μL of SIM to the dissection dish well containing 200 μL fSIM.
Pipette the ovarioles in 5–10 μL fSIM onto a 35 mm FluoroDish glass bottom dish and spread the droplet thin with an eyelash glued to a toothpick.
Position the ovarioles close together using the eyelash tool.
Add 1–2 μL thrombin (10 U/mL) dropwise to form the fibrinogen-thrombin clot.
Cover the FluoroDish and leave for 10 min to allow clot formation at 20°C.
Add 100 μL of iSIM prewarmed to 25°C.
Apply a piece of damp tissue paper to the edge of the dish to prevent drying out.
Set the pinhole to 1 airy unit.
Set the scan speed to 400 Hz unidirectional.
Acquire an image of 512 pixels per line and 256–512 lines at 8 bit.
Use the 488 nm laser excitation line.
Use the 561 nm laser excitation line.
Collect images using hybrid detectors with the white laser set to 70%.
Set 488 nm laser intensity to 10%.
Set 574 nm laser intensity to 5%.
Apply 2× line averaging during image collection.
Acquire z stacks at 0.75 μm intervals.
Acquire 10–20 z stacks continuously.
Ensure all of the germarium or anterior germarium is contained in the z stack acquisition.
Locate germaria on the glass coverslip using brightfield illumination.
Pick a germarium lying relatively flat to the coverslip for imaging.
Use fluorescence illumination to identify the GSCs and niche cells.
Ensure the niche cells are oriented orthogonal to the GSCs.
Set up a time lapse for up to 3 hours.
Open movies in Fiji using Bio-Formats Importer with specified settings.
Adjust the brightness of the images.
Apply an exponential fit bleach correction.
Apply a 0.5x × 0.5y × 0.5z pixel-wide 3D Gaussian blur.
Create a maximum projection z stack and crop as appropriate.
Create a maximum projection z stack to encompass the region/structure of interest.
Crop the image by drawing a rectangle around the region of interest and using the crop function.
Use the line tool to draw over the length of the projection.
Determine the length of the projection using Analyze > Measure.
Save movies as .avi files with the desired number of frames per second.
